findings: Physical tool translation is explicit at about 149.3mm from link6; existing NativeMeasurements only accepts the zero-offset link6 candidate, so a separately gated explicit physical-offset adapter is required.
FragmentExecutor requires a real RUNNING EpisodeLifecycle; diagnostic commands use its DualArmController primitive and the neutral native observer without creating a benchmark lifecycle.

The 0.4m/s default reaches the 0.05rad joint target lead cap at recorded home. Linearized predicted translation is 0.01191m and rotational leakage is about 0.00524rad for that first candidate command; this is an offline prediction, not measured tracking.
The proposed conservative speed ladders are contact0.025/0.05m/s, transit0.10/0.20m/s, angular0.5/1.0rad/s. No setting is selected automatically.
Original head and wrist RGB do not establish an empty gripper region. A generic upward lift and negative initial tool-X retreat precede fresh root/operator visual clearance for any close.
Native close target remains -0.01m although recorded physical finger limits start at0m; measure actual response and stop on the declared observed-limit excess without changing the target.
Free-space contact-profile traces do not validate loaded contact behavior. Empty-gripper timing does not validate grasp-success or maintained-object gap-change thresholds.
Settling sweeps and rolling progress observations are reported from measured25Hz traces; genuine-obstruction stall detection and workspace-wide tracking remain untested.
